en.degreeContext: A third-degree felony ordinarily carries up to 5 years in prison and a $5,000 fine. Under §893.101 lack of knowledge of the substance’s illicit nature is an affirmative defense. If raised, actual or constructive possession permits, but does not require, an inference of that knowledge. This entry covers non-cannabis applications. Cannabis-specific liability and medical-marijuana compliance require separate review. Subsection (6)(a) excludes substances lawfully obtained from a practitioner, under a valid professional prescription or order, or otherwise authorized under the chapter. Section (6)(d) separately grades Schedule V possession as a second-degree misdemeanor, ordinarily up to 60 days and $500. Section (6)(b) addresses up to 20 grams of cannabis excluding extracted resin and its preparations. Section (6)(c) separately addresses over 10 grams of certain listed substances or mixtures. The professional and official exclusions in (9) have their own conditions.
